rules: Hooks and outcomes quote neet-t1-5.json unchanged; journey prose repeats no outcome fact - the false bottom's discovery, the rhyme's lesson entry and mushroom credit, and the rope-lattice legacy (named lattice, zero-loss record, pantry imitation) are owned by the outcome beat alone.
Each journey is self-contained: no scene assumes another route was seen first, and none references Neet's tier-1 routes (shelf rule, bed-ledger correction, loft braces), M1, or any later tier.
The named mushroom drives the problem and its resolution rather than appearing as set dressing.

Voice anchors as in journey-expansion-01: data/visitor-dialogue.json (Neet offer/active/failed lines), drafts/neet.json, and Neet's accepted M1 viewpoints - formal diction, dry understatement, habits written down then quietly crossed out. Added for tier 2: the v1 foraging texture (pre-dew ravine, the cleric's rule) is echoed lightly as established reference lore, inventoried in factProvenance.

routes.hook: The shrine soup pot wants sturdy caps, and the porter's basket always seems lighter on the way back up. Neet decides to weigh the basket once, out of politeness.
routes.journey:
Neet is in the ravine before the dew lifts, on the fallen oaks where sturdy caps grow dense and low. She culls wide clusters and leaves half of every log behind - the cleric's rule keeps itself without a witness - and a dropped cap takes its gravel tumble no worse than a scuff. It survives being carried - what the soup pot pays for.

Harl the porter comes up the switchback, one basket, the pickers' tally slip riding the rim. Neet asks to carry it the last few yards, out of politeness, and the weight reads wrong in her grip. She weighs it once at the kitchen scale, thanking him for the loan, then sets today's beside the delivery weights her ledger has kept for weeks.

'Full at the ravine, lighter by the gate,' Harl says. 'I have been telling my arms they are getting old.' 'The ledger has agreed with you for weeks,' she says. 'A shortfall that keeps its size could come from habit, cargo, or the basket itself, and nothing yet tells me which. I would like to weigh your basket again - may I?'

The apology is drafted for the asking, not for any finding: questioning a guest's basket costs something, and she will pay it. The page takes two columns - what the tally slips promise, what the scale confirms - the second left blank for morning. The pilgrims' soup has waited out worse and can wait for a scale willing to repeat.
routes.outcome: A false bottom has been shorting the count for weeks; she double-counts by weight, catches it kindly, and cooks nothing until every cap is accounted. Jars of sturdy-cap soup go out to the pilgrims, and the twice-counted rule becomes the children's first lesson in counting anything.

plan.mainTask: Turn a week of polite suspicion into a decision Neet can act on: prove the weight to herself without insulting the man who carries it.
plan.secondaryTask: Anchor the dense-cap material texture and the v1 cleric's foraging rule; pre-commit the kindness the outcome's kind catch needs.
plan.povLimit: Neet has the hook's recurring lightness plus the ledger's kept delivery weights and today's scale reading - measured, repeatable evidence of shortfall, no cause. She must not discover or name the false bottom in the journey - the discovery and what it proves are outcome-owned. The reader may suspect; Neet may not.
plan.requiredCharacters: Neet; Harl the porter (witness and unwitting source of the second weighing's need); the kitchen scale as instrument. No other named figures.
plan.requiredInformation: Why one weighing is courtesy and a second is suspicion; that consistency alone proves neither guilt nor innocence; that soup waits for proof.
plan.forbiddenMistakes: Naming the false bottom; accusing Harl; promising the children's rule or the pilgrim jars (both outcome-owned); any route leak.
plan.agency: Experiential center, decision owner, and execution owner: Neet. Harl: witness whose self-doubt requires an announced, apologized-for check rather than a silent audit. The discovery, the kind catch, and the rule are formalized by the outcome beat.

routes.hook: The clever mushrooms present themselves for labeling, which is exactly how Neet knows they are lying. The beds have been acting suspicious all week.
routes.journey:
The clever mushrooms have spent a week presenting themselves: caps curled generously outward, white stems standing to be counted, beds turned toward the path by hands nobody can name. Sedge, who weeds the garden and reports in a flat voice, has watched them all week: too neat to trust.

Neet cuts a set of stakes and carries them out as the obvious, orderly thing. The first never touches soil: the nearest cap folds into the leaf litter flat and final, between one blink and the next, without a sound. She tries the second bed and gets the same shallow theater. 'They only do it when the stakes come out,' Sedge calls from the far row. 'It is not the watching they mind. I stood over them all Tuesday.'

So Neet rolls the label into its leather and stands at the path with her hands folded, and the beds remember themselves - up, curled, guilty. A label nobody will hold still for keeps nothing; the week's refusals are the better record. The patch by the warm stone keeps its distance from the stone; the patch under the drip-line grows nowhere wet. A mushroom that lies about itself still tells the truth about where it will not stand.

She maps the refusals in the day's margin and pencils one line of a rhyme beside them, to hear whether rhythm can keep what stakes cannot: it will not stand where the drip-line lands. The third stake stays in the drawer, on purpose.
routes.outcome: They keep flattening into leaf litter at the first touch of a label, so she stops labeling and starts rhyming, sorting by where they refuse to grow. A basket is collected in order, and the sorting rhyme enters the children's lesson, where it is credited to the mushrooms.

plan.mainTask: Force Neet's record-keeping instinct against a material that refuses labels, and let her read refusal as the data that sorts better than names.
plan.secondaryTask: Stage the flattening as gathered evidence rather than comedy alone; give the volunteer a functional witness role; seed the rhyme as an experiment, not an institution.
plan.povLimit: Neet does not know why the beds are suspicious at hook time; tag-refusal is discovered by test within the journey. The rhyme's adoption as lesson material and its credit to the mushrooms are outcome-owned.
plan.requiredCharacters: Neet; Sedge the weeding volunteer (flat-voiced witness); the beds as antagonist. No other named figures.
plan.requiredInformation: That presentation reads as lying; that the trigger is the stake, not the watcher; that refusals sort better than labels here.
plan.forbiddenMistakes: Claiming the rhyme as instituted practice or crediting it to the mushrooms; any recall of tier-1 Mana (re-ink, bed-ledger correction); turning the mushrooms into persons; any route leak.
plan.agency: Experiential center, decision owner, and execution owner: Neet. Sedge: witness whose flat report supplies the week's pattern. The stop-labeling turn, the rhyming method, the ordered collection, and the lesson entry belong to the outcome beat.

routes.hook: The lively mushrooms have been escaping crates since dawn, and the downhill trip to the village is today. Neet checks the rope twice.
routes.journey:
The lively mushrooms have spent the morning furnishing their own exits: one over the first crate rim before breakfast, two more at the second loading, each landing springy and unrepentant. The downhill trip falls today, and the pantry's pickling day does not move for anyone's manners.

Neet reads the shed's one good rope twice, knot by knot, because she suspects she is about to ask it for everything. The cooper arrives with four lids, already named a favor. 'Nothing gets out of my crates,' he says, which is true and not the point: a lid settles every argument in the dark, and a shortfall keeps its own counsel until the far end. She hands the lids back. 'If one gets out today, it gets out in daylight, where the getting-out has witnesses.'

So the crates ride out open, under rope - spans anchored to the cooper's hoop-nails, woven wide enough to see through. She checks it once at the gate and once at the hairpin, half for the knots, half for the mushrooms, who are owed a fair fence. On the bend one cap takes the bounce as a dare, clears the first span, and is caught by the second.

Past the village's first roofs the crates keep their drumroll, ropes humming at every spring. At the pantry step she sets them down still arguing, and the lids stay home in the shed. A quiet delivery would have been easier on everybody. She does not trust what she cannot watch.
routes.outcome: She lattices the crates with rope - not lids: rope, so the jumping is visible and the failure honest. Not one loss goes on the record, and the village pantry copies her lattice by month's end.

plan.mainTask: Take a public delivery downhill with containment she can defend: rope seen, not lids believed.
plan.secondaryTask: Honor the hook's twice-checked rope as a live opening beat; stage one near-loss caught by the spans; leave the zero-loss line unclaimed.
plan.povLimit: The rope decision predates the hook (she checks the rope twice before the journey opens); the consequential choice staged here is the cooper's last-second lids offer refused in person. The record line and the pantry's imitation are outcome-owned.
plan.requiredCharacters: Neet; the unnamed cooper (pride, lids, concession); the village pantry as destination. No other named figures.
plan.requiredInformation: Why rope instead of lids (failure kept in daylight, under observation); the lattice's physical credibility and the hairpin's danger.
plan.forbiddenMistakes: Claiming 'not one loss on the record' or the pantry's imitation; reusing the outcome's 'visible/honest' phrasing as her own sentence; any route leak.
plan.agency: Experiential center, decision owner, and execution owner: Neet. The cooper: functional opposition whose craft still anchors the rope. Results and legacy belong to the outcome beat.

characterNotes.life: Neet as courteous auditor: she weighs in plain sight, records before concluding, and drafts the apology for the discomfort of the asking before the request even lands - politeness carrying a decision, not concealing it. The two-column page is the shelf-economist habit of the accepted T1 Life journey, grown to face a live suspect rather than a shortage.
characterNotes.mana: Neet as record keeper meeting her limit: a label those beds will not hold still for keeps nothing, so she moves the truth-keeping from wood to rhythm - the Mana branch signature ('the record needs checking') under a material that out-lies ink. The drawer line is her formal mind refusing to treat surrender as an option.
characterNotes.stamina: Neet as defender of witnesses: the building (pantry) and the day need her back on schedule, and she pays for punctuality in publicity - failures happen where people can see. The close ('does not trust what she cannot watch') seeds the outcome's visible-jumping principle without borrowing its wording.

flags: No contradiction with any existing anchor was found in the three hooks/outcomes. The one live tension - the false bottom seems to indict Harl - is handled as an open question inside the journey: her concern rests on measured, repeatable evidence (today's scale reading set beside the ledger's kept delivery weights), the cause is left an open question in her own words, the second weighing is requested as a courtesy ('may I?'), and the apology is drafted for the discomfort of the asking rather than for any finding - which is what keeps the outcome's catch kind.

Route independence: no journey references another route's events, materials, or named figures, any tier-1 outcome, M1, or later tiers - the T1 named side figures (Mena, Gorram) and the other mushrooms are absent from each journey's prose.
Named-NPC risk accepted as in the T1 pilot: two new named figures (Harl, Sedge) and one unnamed (the cooper); no settlement award, no material award, no stamp, and no egg is promised anywhere.

The Stamina hook already has the rope in hand ('checks the rope twice'), so the journey stages the consequential choice as the cooper's final lids offer rather than inventing a first decision after the hook.
